_handoff.scopeNote: Clean-sale e-Khata/EPID dependency baseline. Public official-interface observations are B; the citizen-provided firsthand note is E. Unverified mapping and authenticated EPID-flow requirements remain Unknown.

claims.text: BESCOM's public homepage exposes a service entry labelled Name Change with EPID.
claims.notes: This verifies the public entry only; it does not verify eligibility, backend matching, or post-login fields.

claims.text: BESCOM's FAQ says the standard Name Change/Change of Ownership route redirects the customer to login, then asks the customer to select an account, complete mandatory fields, upload required documents, submit, receive a request ID, and pay applicable charges.
claims.notes: This is a documented standard route and fallback; it does not describe the EPID route.

claims.text: BESCOM's FAQ describes the Account ID as a 10-digit unique number printed on the electricity bill and used for future communication and consumer-portal registration.
claims.notes: This confirms the Account ID's public description, not an EPID mapping rule.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi search supports lookup by SAS property-tax ID, property EPID, ward, or owner name.
claims.notes: A result requires property-specific input and was not attempted.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi search tells a user who cannot find the property to use the Do Not Find My Property eKhata route for corporation review.
The e-Aasthi citizen portal says Draft e-Khata has been issued according to the existing BBMP property-tax register.
claims.notes: Draft existence is not evidence that ownership has been updated or that the record is final.

claims.text: The e-Aasthi citizen portal lists a registered deed, Aadhaar-based eKYC, SAS property-tax application number, property photo, and A-Khata-supporting documents as information to upload for Final e-Khata; it says an encumbrance certificate is needed when immediate sale or transfer is planned.
claims.notes: The public page lists inputs, not a guaranteed processing outcome or a universal mutation sequence.

claims.text: The e-Aasthi citizen portal publicly offers eKhata Automatic Mutations—Get Your Mutation.
claims.notes: Public availability of the route does not verify an individual property's eligibility or automatic completion.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi Pending Mutation Report labels a workflow as Aadhaar based Automatic Mutation and displays fields for date of registered deed or mutation application, basis of mutation, property EPID, seller/giving-party name, purchaser/receiving-party name, and pending owner.
claims.notes: This observes exposed report fields. It does not establish that every registered sale automatically mutates.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi application-status page accepts an EPID to show e-Khata application status.
The firsthand e-Khata note identifies a possible failure in matching a BESCOM Account ID to an EPID even when an e-Khata record exists.
claims.notes: One firsthand signal only; it is not evidence of a published interface contract, cause, or universal rule.

claims.text: For a clean sale, a prudent working hypothesis is registered sale deed, municipal mutation/final-record resolution in the buyer's name, usable EPID, then BESCOM transfer; the official sources verify portions of this chain but not this end-to-end dependency.
claims.notes: Official sources verify the municipal inputs/routes and BESCOM entry; the end-to-end order and mapping dependency are inference, prompted by the firsthand note.

claims.text: The public materials reviewed do not document the Name Change with EPID route's exact Account-ID↔EPID validation, identity-document, payment, agreement, e-sign, approval, or bill-update steps.
claims.notes: Do not import detailed authenticated-flow assertions from community reports as official requirements. Fresh public/authenticated evidence is needed.

nodes.label: Registered sale deed
nodes.summary: Registered property-transfer document available to support Final e-Khata inputs; it is not by itself proof that a mutation or BESCOM transfer completed.
nodes.requiredState: A registered deed is available where the Final e-Khata route requests it.

checks.label: Final e-Khata input
checks.description: The public e-Aasthi portal lists a registered deed among Final e-Khata uploads.

failureSignals.label: Deed unavailable
failureSignals.description: No public source reviewed supplies a recovery rule for a missing deed in this chain.

recoveries.label: Use the municipal record route
recoveries.description: Use the official Final e-Khata guidance to identify its listed deed requirement; property-specific recovery is not evidenced here.

nodes.label: Municipal mutation
nodes.summary: e-Aasthi exposes an Automatic Mutations route and a report connecting mutation data with registered deeds, party names, EPID, and a pending owner.
nodes.requiredState: The applicable municipal ownership/mutation record has reached the buyer-facing state required for the next route; automatic completion is not assumed.

checks.label: Automatic mutation route
checks.description: The citizen portal exposes eKhata Automatic Mutations—Get Your Mutation.

checks.label: Mutation report fields
checks.description: The public report shows deed/mutation date, basis, EPID, seller, purchaser, and pending owner fields.

failureSignals.label: Mutation pending
failureSignals.description: A mutation can remain with a named pending owner in the public report; do not infer completion from deed registration alone.

recoveries.label: Check mutation route/status
recoveries.description: Use the official Automatic Mutations entry and EPID status page; no property-specific request was submitted.

nodes.label: Final e-Khata
nodes.summary: Municipal record state after the draft/final process; a Draft record is explicitly derived from the existing property-tax register and must not be presented as buyer-name confirmation.
nodes.requiredState: A Final e-Khata state whose displayed ownership is suitable for the buyer's transfer route; public sources reviewed do not establish a universal final-state test.

checks.label: Final e-Khata guidance
checks.description: The citizen portal lists uploads for getting Final e-Khata, including registered deed and eKYC.

checks.label: EPID status
checks.description: The public status page accepts EPID for e-Khata application status.

failureSignals.label: Draft e-Khata
failureSignals.description: A Draft e-Khata is based on the existing BBMP property-tax register; it may therefore fail to prove the buyer-facing final record required by the inferred clean-sale chain.

failureSignals.label: Seller or builder remains recorded
failureSignals.description: Public mutation fields distinguish giving and receiving parties, but no public source reviewed proves when BESCOM accepts or rejects a different owner name.

recoveries.label: Follow Final e-Khata guidance
recoveries.description: Use the official final-record guidance and required uploads; do not assume a draft will be upgraded automatically.

nodes.label: Property EPID
nodes.summary: Municipal property identifier that the public e-Aasthi search and application-status interfaces accept.
nodes.requiredState: The property can be located by EPID or a public alternate lookup, and the EPID can be used for municipal status checks.

checks.label: Public property search
checks.description: Search by property EPID, SAS property-tax ID, ward, or owner name.

checks.label: Application status
checks.description: Enter EPID to view e-Khata application status.

failureSignals.label: Property not found
failureSignals.description: The search interface offers a dedicated route when the property is not found.

recoveries.label: Use missing-property route
recoveries.description: Use Do Not Find My Property eKhata for corporation review; no submission was made.

nodes.label: BESCOM Account-ID to EPID mapping
nodes.summary: Unpublished interface relationship between the 10-digit BESCOM Account ID and the municipal EPID, if the EPID service uses such a match.
nodes.requiredState: A property-specific mapping succeeds in the Name Change with EPID route; public evidence of the validation, owner, and repair process is absent.

checks.label: Account ID available
checks.description: The BESCOM FAQ says Account ID is 10 digits and printed on the bill.

checks.label: EPID entry exposed
checks.description: BESCOM's homepage exposes Name Change with EPID.

failureSignals.label: Mapping does not resolve
failureSignals.description: A firsthand note identifies this possible failure; exact public error text and repair owner are not verified.

recoveries.label: Use documented standard transfer route
recoveries.description: BESCOM documents Name Change/Change of Ownership using login, account selection, mandatory fields, document upload, submission, request ID, and payment.

nodes.label: BESCOM name transfer
nodes.summary: BESCOM exposes both a standard Name Change/Change of Ownership flow and a public Name Change with EPID entry; their equivalence and EPID route requirements are not documented by reviewed public sources.
nodes.requiredState: A request is completed under the applicable BESCOM route; the Name Change with EPID post-login requirements and completion evidence are unknown.

checks.label: Standard transfer guidance
checks.description: The FAQ documents customer login, account selection, fields, documents, request ID, and payment for Name Change/Change of Ownership.

checks.label: EPID route entry
checks.description: The homepage publicly exposes Name Change with EPID.

failureSignals.label: EPID route cannot be completed from public evidence
failureSignals.description: The reviewed public material does not disclose exact EPID validation, identity, payment, agreement, e-sign, approval, or bill-update steps.

recoveries.label: Choose the documented standard route when appropriate
recoveries.description: Use the standard BESCOM Name Change/Change of Ownership route and its official request tracking; eligibility against EPID-route failures remains unverified.

nodes.label: Updated BESCOM bill
nodes.summary: A bill showing the new consumer's name is the practical downstream confirmation, but no reviewed public source documents the timing or display condition after the EPID route.
nodes.requiredState: A future bill/account display shows the updated name; source and timing remain to be evidenced.

failureSignals.label: No documented post-transfer confirmation
failureSignals.description: No reviewed official public source specifies when or where an EPID-route name update appears after approval.

edges.label: Registered-deed information is exposed in the municipal mutation workflow; universal automatic completion is not established.
A buyer-facing final municipal record is a prudent inferred dependency, not a published universal rule.
Final-record and EPID relationship is a working hypothesis; the public interface separately supports EPID lookup/status.
BESCOM exposes an EPID transfer entry, but its Account-ID mapping contract is not publicly documented in reviewed material.
A successful EPID mapping appears necessary for the EPID route; the standard document route is an officially documented alternative.
Expected downstream confirmation; timing and display are not documented by reviewed evidence.

roadblocks.title: Draft e-Khata is not a verified buyer-facing final record
roadblocks.symptom: A property has a Draft e-Khata but the clean-sale chain cannot establish a final record in the buyer's name.
roadblocks.likelyCause: The portal says draft e-Khata was issued from the existing property-tax register; it does not prove current ownership or finality.
roadblocks.recovery: Use the official Final e-Khata guidance and EPID status route; supply only the listed documents through the official flow, not through this research process.

roadblocks.title: Property cannot be found in public e-Khata search
roadblocks.symptom: The property cannot be located using available public e-Aasthi lookup paths.
roadblocks.likelyCause: The public interface identifies a missing-property state but does not expose a property-specific cause without input.
roadblocks.recovery: Use the official Do Not Find My Property eKhata route for corporation review; do not submit personal data in the ledger.

roadblocks.title: Municipal record still presents a prior owner
roadblocks.symptom: A mutation record may retain a seller/giving party, purchaser/receiving party, or pending-owner state rather than a confirmed buyer-facing final record.
roadblocks.likelyCause: Mutation/report data are not the same as verified final ownership for the BESCOM EPID route; exact acceptance behavior is undocumented.
roadblocks.recovery: Check the official mutation and EPID-status routes, then use Final e-Khata guidance where applicable. If the EPID route remains unusable, consider BESCOM's separately documented standard name-change route.

roadblocks.title: EPID does not resolve to the intended BESCOM account
roadblocks.symptom: An EPID and BESCOM Account ID are available but the EPID transfer route cannot establish the expected match.
roadblocks.likelyCause: One firsthand note identifies this possible integration failure; public sources reviewed do not disclose matching rules, error text, repair owner, or SLA.
roadblocks.recovery: Do not repeatedly submit. Preserve non-sensitive error wording, use BESCOM's official support/standard name-change guidance, and obtain fresh official evidence before claiming a mapping repair procedure.

journeys.title: Clean sale: municipal record toward BESCOM EPID transfer
journeys.context: Partial reconstructed journey for Bengaluru. Official public interfaces verify municipal search/status/mutation entry points and BESCOM service entries; the full EPID transaction is not observed or submitted.

steps.label: Keep the registered deed available
steps.action: Check the official Final e-Khata guidance for its listed deed input.
steps.expectedResult: The deed is available for the municipal record route, without assuming any downstream state.

steps.label: Inspect municipal mutation state
steps.action: Use the public e-Aasthi mutation entry/report and, where available, the official status path.
steps.expectedResult: The user can distinguish a published route/report from a completed buyer-facing record.

steps.label: Resolve final e-Khata state
steps.action: Follow the official Final e-Khata document guidance; do not treat Draft as final buyer-name confirmation.
steps.expectedResult: A final municipal record state may be established, but its precise BESCOM acceptance condition is unknown.

steps.label: Locate EPID and inspect status
steps.action: Use official public e-Aasthi search/status interfaces, or the dedicated missing-property route.
steps.expectedResult: An EPID/status route or explicit missing-property recovery is visible.

steps.label: Assess BESCOM EPID match
steps.action: Use no personal data in research; record this as a property-specific operational check in the public EPID entry.
steps.expectedResult: The exact match result and repair path remain unknown until fresh official evidence exists.

steps.label: Use the appropriate BESCOM transfer route
steps.action: The public homepage exposes Name Change with EPID; BESCOM separately documents the standard Name Change/Change of Ownership workflow.
steps.expectedResult: A documented fallback exists, while EPID-route requirements/approval are unknown.

steps.label: Confirm later bill/account display
steps.action: Check for a future official account/bill name update only after transfer completion.
steps.expectedResult: No timing or confirmation source is yet evidenced.

dependencies.description: The municipal report connects registered-deed/mutation data to EPID and parties, without proving a universal automatic outcome.
Buyer-facing final-record resolution is inferred as a clean-sale prerequisite; public material does not publish the full rule.
EPID is publicly searchable/status-checkable, but its exact production from finalisation is not established.
BESCOM exposes a Name Change with EPID entry, while the Account-ID mapping contract is unknown.
A mapping success is inferred for the EPID route; standard document-based transfer is separately documented.

recoveryNotes: Use the official e-Aasthi missing-property and status routes before assuming a BESCOM-only failure.
Treat BESCOM's documented standard Name Change/Change of Ownership flow as a separate fallback, not proof that the EPID route is identical.
Keep account IDs, EPIDs, addresses, identity documents, login data, OTPs, and screenshots with personal data out of the ledger.
documentationQualityNotes: Municipal public interfaces expose search, status, mutation, and final-record guidance with concrete fields and routes.
BESCOM publicly exposes Name Change with EPID but reviewed public materials do not document its workflow or Account-ID↔EPID matching behavior.
The only mapping-failure signal in this baseline is a firsthand note, so it is retained as E/partial and not elevated to official evidence.
